# Vīrakajātaka (Ja 204)

**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

**Title (Pali):** Vīrakajātaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The Crow Named Heroic

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vīrakajātaka* (Ja 204) is a canonical birth story belonging to the Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. The Buddha delivered the teaching while residing at Jetavana regarding Devadatta's presumptuous attempt to imitate the Buddha (*sugatālaya*) by trying to preach the Dhamma flanked by chief disciples [SuttaCentral; Burlingame 1921; Fausböll 1879]. Declaring that Devadatta had previously met destruction through imitation, the Buddha recounts a past birth in which the Bodhisatta was born as a water-bird or water-crow named Vīraka, and Devadatta was a city crow named Saviṭṭhaka [Burlingame 1921; Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1879].

In the story, Saviṭṭhaka leaves his home, enters the service of Vīraka, and attempts to dive into water to catch fish in imitation of his master [Burlingame 1921; Anandajoti 2010]. Unable to navigate the water, Saviṭṭhaka becomes entangled in waterweeds (*sevāla*) and drowns [Burlingame 1921; Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1879]. When Saviṭṭhaka's mate arrives inquiring after her sweet-voiced husband with a neck like a peacock (*mayūragīvasaṅkāsa*), Vīraka answers with a verse revealing that the crow perished attempting to emulate a bird that moves both on water and on land [Burlingame 1921; Fausböll 1879]. Anandajoti summarizes the core theme of the Jātaka as "keeping to one's own habitat" [Anandajoti 2010].

No internal Pali text reuse or cross-language parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora are listed by SuttaCentral or detected in DharmaNexus machine alignments [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. The narrative and verses of the Jātaka are, however, preserved in the Jātaka commentary and also cited within the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* [Burlingame 1921; Fausböll 1879].
